plan_title: Subpart RR Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) Plan Barnett RDC #1 Wise County, Texas
ama_definition: The AMA is set equal to the MMA (the 50-year post-injection stabilized plume plus a half-mile buffer), which the plan says exceeds the 98.449 superposition of year-14 and year-19 plume areas (p35).
mma_definition: The modeled free-phase CO2 plume (5% molar cutoff) at its stabilized extent 50 years after a 12-year injection period, plus a half-mile buffer; about 4.28 square miles, reaching 1.62 miles from the injector (p34).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: Only surface equipment is rated 'possible' (<100 MT per event); well penetrations and surface equipment are named as the only existing pathways, while existing/future wells, faults and fractures, confining layers, seismicity and lateral migration are rated improbable (p34-35, p45).
baseline_summary: Mixed: operational SCADA data used to flag deviations from expected performance; pre-injection baseline groundwater quality from one new groundwater well sampled by a third-party lab; baseline seismicity from historical USGS and TexNet catalogs augmented by dCarbon's own array. Baseline data to be collected before injection begins (p53, p57).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report with the mass balance (Equations RR-5, RR-10, RR-12) and any leakage estimates with methodology; leak quantities and composition variation to be included in recurring regulatory filings; records kept at least three years. Leaks managed per Texas regulations and TRRC permit conditions, but no explicit commitment to publish measurement data or report monitoring results to the state (p37, p47, p49-50, p54-56, p59).

rows.detail: Three meters: orifice or Coriolis meter at the Bridgeport Plant interface (gas phase), Coriolis meter after compression, and Coriolis meter at the wellsite upstream of the wellhead; gas chromatograph at wellsite; samples at least quarterly.
rows.location: Bridgeport Plant interface, compression facility outlet, and injection well site
rows.trigger_or_response: Discrepancies between meters investigated and reconciled; unaccounted CO2 quantified per Subpart W and subtracted from injection.
rows.evidence_quote: CO2 for injection will be metered in three locations for redundancy and precision.

rows.detail: Continuous collection of injection volumes, pressures, temperatures and gas composition via SCADA and automated systems; wellhead pressure/temperature gauges; surface pressure kept below 0.50 psi/ft gradient and permit maximum 4,500 psig.
rows.location: Barnett RDC #1 wellhead and compression facility
rows.trigger_or_response: Data outside acceptable performance limits: qualified personnel review and follow response and reporting procedures; abnormal pressure concerns lead to shut-in and investigation.
rows.evidence_quote: dCarbon will continuously monitor and collect injection volumes, pressures, temperatures, and gas composition data for the injection well.

rows.detail: Downhole pressure and temperature gauges near the bottom of the tubing monitor the tubing-casing annulus as well as the injection stream.
rows.trigger_or_response: Change in annulus pressure indicates a possible leak requiring remediation.
rows.evidence_quote: The downhole gauges will monitor the inside of the tubing (injection stream) as well as the annulus.

rows.detail: Annual mechanical integrity tests of the injection well; well constructed with three casing strings cemented to surface and a tubing/packer completion.
rows.trigger_or_response: Negative MIT: well immediately isolated and leak mitigated.
rows.evidence_quote: Mechanical Integrity Tests (MITs) performed annually would also indicate the presence of a leak.

rows.detail: Bottomhole pressure gauges installed before injection to monitor reservoir pressure; periodic pressure fall-off tests to watch for unexpected static pressure increases; initial PFOT during well construction to check model assumptions.
rows.location: Barnett RDC #1 injection well (Ellenburger subunit E)
rows.trigger_or_response: Unexpected formation pressure increase: fault slip potential analysis; if concern remains, shut in well and investigate; update reservoir model with new data.
rows.evidence_quote: dCarbon plans to perform periodic pressure fall-off tests (PFOT) to determine and monitor reservoir pressure

rows.detail: Daily auditory, visual and olfactory (AVO) inspections of gauges, monitors and leak indicators at the compressor facility and injection well, looking for vapor clouds, ice and abnormal observations.
rows.location: Compressor facility, pipeline and injection well site
rows.trigger_or_response: Vapor clouds, ice or abnormal AVO/FLIR observations: corrective action, often immediate repair of valves/flanges; leaked CO2 quantified and reported.
rows.evidence_quote: field personnel conduct daily AVO field inspections of gauges, monitors, and leak indicators.

rows.detail: All BKV and dCarbon field personnel wear personal H2S monitors alarming at about 1 ppm; H2S in the stream serves as the indicator of a CO2 leak.
rows.trigger_or_response: Alarm: immediate response to protect personnel, verify monitors, secure facility; release mass calculated from operating conditions.
rows.evidence_quote: all dCarbon and BKV field personnel are required to wear H2S monitors, which will trigger the alarm at low levels of H2S

rows.detail: Facility and well monitored for H2S and CO2 concentration increases with high-alarm setpoints; gas detectors run continuously except for maintenance/calibration; recurring FLIR leak surveys of compressor, pipeline and well.
rows.location: Compression facility and injection well site; pipeline for FLIR surveys
rows.trigger_or_response: High H2S alarm automatically alerts field personnel; release treated as major upset and mass calculated from pressure, flow, leak size and duration.
rows.evidence_quote: The facility and well will be monitored for H2S and CO2 concentration increases.

rows.detail: Soil flux detectors listed among emerging technologies dCarbon may evaluate for quantifying a detected leak; no commitment.
rows.evidence_quote: dCarbon may also evaluate other emerging technologies for quantifying CO2 leakage such as non-dispersive infra-red (NDIR) CO2 sensors and soil flux detectors.

rows.detail: One new groundwater monitoring well near the injection site, deeper than local water wells, sampled periodically for chemical composition; baseline established by third-party laboratory before injection.
rows.location: One monitoring well in the MMA near the injection well
rows.trigger_or_response: Increase in groundwater CO2 over baseline: analyzed volumetrically for a preliminary leakage estimate.
rows.evidence_quote: dCarbon plans to install a deep groundwater monitoring well in the MMA that will be used to monitor the USDW.

rows.detail: Cement bond logs on the three casing strings during well construction to verify integrity; a construction QA step, not a repeat monitoring log.
rows.evidence_quote: Each of these three casing strings will be cemented to the surface and inspected with cement bond logs to ensure wellbore integrity.

rows.detail: dCarbon will install its own ground seismic monitoring array near the injection site and also follow the public TexNet network; events located and analyzed for origin and effect on confining layers.
rows.location: Dedicated array near the injection site plus TexNet
rows.trigger_or_response: Event of magnitude 3.0 or greater: review injection volumes and pressures for changes indicating leakage; abnormal seismicity concern leads to shut-in and investigation.
rows.evidence_quote: dCarbon plans to install new ground seismic monitoring arrays near the injection site that are designed to detect any seismic events in the area

rows.detail: Existing dCarbon 3D seismic used to interpret faults and karst for site characterization; no repeat seismic survey planned.
rows.evidence_quote: No faulting is interpreted in the MMA around the Barnett RDC #1 based on available subsurface data including 3D seismic data.

rows.detail: Ambient CO2 sensing, UAV-mounted ppb CO2 sensor flown over the MMA, eddy covariance, open-path tunable diode lasers and closed-path detectors discussed as options to quantify a detected leak ('could', 'will consider').
rows.trigger_or_response: Deviations from an ambient baseline, paired with meteorological and PVT data, would be used to attribute and estimate leak rates.
rows.evidence_quote: atmospheric sensing technology could be used to establish a baseline of ambient CO2 concentration in the project area and identify any fluctuations.

rows.detail: Subpart W calculation methods for equipment leaks and vents between the injection meter and wellhead; detected releases quantified from pressure, flow rate, leak opening size and duration; direct leak surveys avoided because of H2S.
rows.location: Surface equipment between flow meter and wellhead
rows.evidence_quote: Calculation methods from Subpart W will be used to calculate CO2 emissions from equipment located on the surface

rows.detail: Quarterly review of TRRC records for proposed and approved drilling permits within the MMA to catch new wells that could create pathways.
rows.trigger_or_response: New well proposed, permitted or drilled: investigate added risk and update the MRV plan.
rows.evidence_quote: dCarbon will reverify the status and public information for all proposed and approved drilling permits within the MMA quarterly.

rows.detail: Internal and external corrosion control program checked by periodic inspection of the pipeline system and analysis of liquids collected from the line.
rows.evidence_quote: monitored through the periodic inspection of the system and analysis of liquids collected from the line.

rows.detail: Fault slip potential analysis (model built from drilling data) if unexpected formation pressure rise is detected; reservoir model, forecasts and MRV plan updated if PFOT or logging show deviations.
rows.trigger_or_response: Unexpected pressure increase: run FSP analysis; if concern remains, shut in and investigate.
rows.evidence_quote: Should any unexpected increase in formation pressure be detected, dCarbon can perform Fault Slip Potential (FSP) analysis

rows.detail: If leakage into existing or future wells is suspected, dCarbon would work with their operators to take wellhead gas samples and compare CO2 against historical or baseline concentrations.
rows.location: Third-party oil and gas wells within the MMA
rows.trigger_or_response: Measurable CO2 increase attributable to injection: estimate by engineering methods, report, subtract from injection; consider workovers or remedial cement.
rows.evidence_quote: take wellhead gas samples to quantify variations or increases of CO2 compared with historical or baseline CO2 concentrations

notes: Figure pages are largely images but monitoring sections are complete in text; Attachments A and B (permits, legacy well records) are referenced but not included. Monitoring period is 12 years of injection plus two post-injection years (p35, p46). Frequencies for annulus pressure and the seismic array are coded 'continuous' because they are permanent downhole gauges/arrays described alongside continuous automated monitoring, but the plan does not state a frequency for them explicitly. Reservoir_pressure baseline marked 'unclear': a pressure fall-off test during construction will check model assumptions and later periodic PFOTs look for unexpected increases, but the plan does not call the first test a baseline. Atmospheric methods (UAV CO2 sensor, eddy covariance, open-path lasers, fixed CO2 systems from an environmental services vendor) are described at length as possible quantification tools using 'could' and 'will consider' language, so coded mentioned_only rather than conditional. FLIR leak surveys are folded into fixed_gas_detectors per the coding convention; their frequency is 'recurring' with no number. Groundwater: the plan commits to one new 'deep' groundwater monitoring well near the injection site, not a network; shallow TDS data will also be collected once during drilling (p20). Production_monitoring is not_found because this is a disposal well with no production (p54). Cement bond logs are a construction QA step, coded mentioned_only.
